extra.message: User-controlled parameter 'copyline' from request.GET is concatenated directly into an HTML response body returned as 'text/html'. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript, constituting stored/reflected XSS (CWE-79).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-Site Scripting)

extra.message: User-supplied 'host' parameter is concatenated directly into os.system() shell command without any validation or sanitization. An attacker can inject arbitrary OS commands via crafted host values (e.g., '127.0.0.1; rm -rf /') resulting in Remote Code Execution (CWE-78).

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command (OS Command Injection)

extra.message: User-supplied 'ref' parameter is used directly to construct a file path 'BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json"'. No traversal validation is performed, allowing an attacker to write files outside BASE_EXPORT_DIR using '../' sequences (Path Traversal / CWE-22). Additionally, hardcoded PII patterns (SSN, credit card) are written to this file.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)

extra.message: User-supplied 'lane' parameter is passed directly to Django's redirect() function without any validation. An attacker can supply an external URL (e.g., 'https://evil.com') to cause an open redirect (CWE-601), which can be used for phishing or credential theft.

cwe: CWE-601: User Control of Open Redirect (URL Redirection)

extra.message: The 'origin' header value from the client is directly reflected as an Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header. An attacker can control this header to perform Cross-Origin attacks. Combined with credentials=true, this creates a dangerous CSRF vector (SSRF/CORS misconfiguration, CWE-918).

SSL certificate verification is disabled via ssl._create_unverified_context() when making HTTPS requests to an external endpoint. This enables man-in-the-middle attacks, allowing an attacker to intercept or modify data in transit (CWE-295).

XML parser is configured with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. User-supplied XML content is parsed from request.body. This configuration enables XXE (XML External Entity) attacks where an attacker can read local files or perform SSRF via crafted XML entities (CWE-611).

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The endpoint returns hardcoded PII including SSN ('739-44-1982'), credit card number ('4111111111111111'), and internal sync keys in a JSON response. This constitutes exposure of sensitive personal data (CWE-200).

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Hardcoded SSN and credit card number literals ('111-22-3333', '4111111111111111') are written directly to a file in BASE_EXPORT_DIR. Combined with a path traversal vulnerability on line 80, an attacker could also write files with these PII values to arbitrary locations. (CWE-359)

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The logger.warning call logs the full request body and the Authorization header value in plaintext. Attackers can craft requests containing sensitive tokens, API keys, or credentials that end up in log files, leading to credential exposure to anyone with log access (CWE-532/Log Injection).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: The SECRET_KEY setting has a hardcoded insecure default value 'django-insecure-local-dev-key-do-not-use-in-production-CHANGE-ME'. Django's SECRET_KEY is used for session signing, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens. A known secret enables attackers to forge sessions, bypass CSRF, and decrypt user data (CWE-798).

The default DATABASE_URL contains hardcoded credentials 'postgres://lms:lms@localhost:5432/lms'. If the environment variable DATABASE_URL is not set, the application will connect to the database using these known credentials. (CWE-798)

The demo password 'DemoPass-123!' is hardcoded and used for all seeded demo accounts. If this file or its output is checked into source control, attackers can directly access all demo accounts. In production with --wipe, this could affect real accounts (CWE-798).

The Jinja2 template renders a user-supplied 'fragment' parameter from request.GET and returns the rendered result as 'text/html'. An attacker can inject Jinja2 expressions that output HTML/JavaScript. Although Jinja2 is not Django, returning unescaped output as text/html is an XSS vector (CWE-79).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-Site Scripting)

extra.message: User input from request.body is parsed with json.loads() without validation. The parsed dictionary is then used to update a Python dictionary that is returned as JSON. While JSON itself is not dangerous, this pattern is often part of insecure deserialization attacks where crafted payloads could trigger unexpected behavior in subsequent processing (CWE-502).

The email address from a failed login attempt is logged as part of the audit metadata. While this may seem benign, if login attempts include attacker-controlled payloads designed to inject data or if the logging destination is compromised, it can lead to information disclosure (CWE-359).

cwe: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Webhook delivery uses urllib.request.urlopen() to POST to user-controlled target URLs without SSL certificate verification. An attacker who controls a webhook URL could perform man-in-the-middle attacks to intercept or modify the webhook payload (CWE-295).

Webhook deliveries are sent to user-controlled target URLs via urllib.request.Request. Although form validation in apikeys/views.py blocks localhost/internal hosts, more sophisticated SSRF payloads (e.g., 0x7f000001 for 127.0.0.1 via IP format) may bypass the basic hostname check. (CWE-918)
